name: DSH Go
tagline: An Android app that runs DeepSeek's AI assistant on your phone or remote-controls it on your desktop.
sentence: Puts DeepSeek Harness (DeepSeek's coding assistant) in your pocket - run it locally on Android without root access, or connect to your desktop and keep working from anywhere.

board.say: Your AI coding assistant is stuck on your desktop - you can't check on it or give it new tasks from your phone.
You open the app on your Android phone.
A chat message, a voice command, or a connection to your desktop's DeepSeek coding assistant.
Runs the AI assistant locally on your phone or connects to your desktop over a secure link.
steps: Runs the DeepSeek engine in a bundled Linux environment on your phone (no root needed), or connects to your desktop over SSH (a secure remote link)
Sends your request to the AI provider you configured
Shows approval cards for sensitive actions - payments and passwords always need your OK

board.say: Your AI assistant, accessible from your pocket.

outputs.eg: Continue a coding conversation from your phone while waiting for coffee
Connect to your desktop's AI agent from your phone and start a new task without walking back to your desk

before: You leave your desk and your coding assistant sits idle until you get back
Checking on a running task means walking back to your computer
after: Continue AI conversations from your phone, or remote-control your desktop's agent from anywhere
Sensitive actions (payments, passwords, shell commands) show an approval card before running
uses_note: DSH Go is 12 days old. No independent user reports have been published yet.

coverage.title: DSH Go Brings DeepSeek's Coding Agent to Android Without Root Access
Run DeepSeek Harness on Android: DSH Go Lets You Remote-Control Desktop AI Agents

steps: Download the APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go/releases/latest) (or [go.dshtui.com/download](https://go.dshtui.com/download)) and install it on your Android phone
On first launch, choose Local (installs a Linux environment, needs about 1 GB) or Remote (connect to a desktop DeepSeek Harness over SSH)
Configure your AI provider and start chatting - or enable phone control under permissions
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go
Then: Download the APK from the Releases page, install it, choose Local mode, and start a chat. 10 minutes (the first-time Linux setup adds a few minutes).

footprint.disk: About 1 GB for the local engine. The offline speech model adds 241 MB.
footprint.memory: no data found. Low-memory devices should use Remote mode (connects to a desktop instead of running locally).
footprint.runs_on: Android 8.0+ (arm64). An x86_64 build is available for emulators. iOS and HarmonyOS are planned but not yet available.

best_for: Anyone who uses DeepSeek Harness and wants to check on it from their phone
Android users who want an AI assistant that runs locally without root access
People who work away from their desk and want to keep their coding agent running
skip_if: You use an iPhone - there's no iOS version yet
You don't use DeepSeek Harness - this app is built specifically for it
You're uncomfortable with an unofficial app that sends screen data to an AI provider

alternatives.name: T3 Code
alternatives.line: Controls multiple coding agents (Claude, Codex, Grok) from your phone or browser - not just DeepSeek

alternatives.name: OpenMausBot
alternatives.line: A desktop chat app where each contact is an AI bot - runs on Mac, Windows and Linux, not mobile

watch: **Unofficial.** DSH Go is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek. It's a community-built client.
**Anonymous usage statistics are on by default.** You can turn them off in Settings, but they're collecting data until you do.
**Screen data may be sent to the AI provider.** When phone control is enabled, screenshots and screen text go to the model you configured.
**Chinese phone brands may kill the background process.** Xiaomi, Huawei, and similar brands aggressively close background apps. The app links to workaround settings, but it's an extra step.
